proposed_fix.description: Confirm CPU saturation/throttling on emailservice and, if confirmed, raise the CPU limit on that container in a gated, reversible change.
steps: Check the emailservice pods' CPU usage versus requests/limits and the container_cpu_cfs_throttled metrics to confirm throttling or saturation.
Check whether the CPU spike coincides with a deploy, config change, or load increase (e.g., more email-send requests from checkout) and with the latency rise in E1.
Check node-level CPU headroom and kernel version for the node hosting emailservice, per R3.
If throttling is confirmed and the node has headroom, raise the CPU limit (and request if it is clearly under-sized) on the emailservice container only, after human approval.
Watch emailservice_cpu, latency-50/90, and cartservice latency for 10-15 minutes after the change to verify recovery.
If the CPU is high because of a runaway process or a bad release, escalate to the owning team or roll back the release instead of just adding CPU.
preconditions: Human approval obtained for any change to resource limits.
Throttling or CPU saturation on emailservice is confirmed from pod/container metrics, not just inferred.
Node has unallocated CPU capacity for the larger limit.
Current resource spec/manifest is saved so it can be restored.
proposed_fix.rollback: Revert the emailservice CPU limit/request to the previously saved values (e.g., re-apply the prior manifest or kubectl rollout undo) and confirm the pod restarts cleanly.
